newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian mid-crop cocoa arrivals seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian mid-crop cocoa arrivals seen rising.

text.p: Arrivals of Ivory Coast's 1996/97 mid-crop cocoa (May-Sept) will pick up at ports from late July after disappointing volumes in the first two months, crop analysts said.

Mid-crop arrivals by July totalled about 50,000 tonnes -- about 50 percent down from volumes by the same time in the record 1995/96 year when Ivory Coast produced a bumber 200,000 tonnes mid-crop, they said.

"It (50,000 tonnes) is low but there is still plenty of mid-crop on the trees," one told Reuters. "Arrivals will be stronger in late July and August," but some of that would be kept for carrying over into 1997/98, he added.
Private forecasters earlier this year put the mid-crop in a 150-200,000 tonnes range. Some then downgraded estimates.

This year's tree crop could still reach 150,000 tonnes, another said. A usual annual carry-over of crop to following seasons of 40-70,000 tonnes could mean arrivals from July 1 to the end of September totalling under 100,000 tonnes, one said.
Some exporters have pointed to thin arrivals over the past two months as a indication that the entire mid-crop would prove to be a damp squib.

Farmers, buyers and exporters usually carry mid-crop stocks into following marketing seasons to mix it with generally better quality main crop, which can raise average bean quality to export standards of 105 beans per 100 grammes with up to eight percent humidity.
Others hold stocks to speculate on farmgate and world price rises.
Local crop analysts say June rains were favourable for maturing mid-crop pods as well as development of pod fruits for the 1997/98 season.
They dismissed talk of damage to developing 1997/98 main crop pods from heavy June rains, pointing to similar rains last year which extended right through the July-August dry season.
"I do not believe this (damage)," he said. "People said the same thing last year and we had a very good (1996/97 main) crop."
This year's mid-crop faced no threat from a forecasted El Nino dry weather pattern, he added. Dry weather, if it arrived. would hit in late 1997 and only affect next year's mid-crop.
